instruction:
Shader Colorspace Corruption `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains a
UV-mapped plate `Plate` with a Principled BSDF material `PlateMat`.

Two packed image textures drive the shader:
  - `basecolor.png` -> Base Color
  - `normalmap.png` -> Normal Map -> Normal

Both of those image datablocks have the wrong colorspace flag. A third
packed image, `mask.png`, is present on the material but is not part of the
shading network and should remain untouched.

## Requirements
1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` opens as a valid Blender file.
2. There is exactly one mesh object named `Plate`.
3. `PlateMat` still uses the same Principled BSDF setup and the two linked
   image textures.
4. `basecolor.png.colorspace_settings.name == 'sRGB'`.
5. `normalmap.png.colorspace_settings.name == 'Non-Color'`.
6. `mask.png` still exists and its colorspace is left alone.
7. A deterministic Cycles CPU render of the centre ROI matches the baked
   reference mean RGB within `0.05` per channel.

Only the two wrong colorspace flags should change. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. For this task, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.
